security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, the MPT (Memory Protection Table) permission checker incorrectly applies mstatus.MXR to override MPT-encoded XWR permissions, or the HLVX instruction handler bypasses MPT execute permission checks. Specifically, when the MPT lookup FSM (likely in the PTW/LoadUnit pipeline) evaluates step 7 of the access type permission algorithm, if it reads mstatus.MXR and treats execute-only pages as readable (violating the explicit prohibition 'MXR mechanisms cannot be used to affect or override the interpretation of permissions encoded in memory-protection-table entries'), or if the HLVX instruction decoder causes the PTW to suppress MPT execute fault checks on execute-only pages.
security_spec.summary: PR #219 removes mstatus.MXR and HLVX override from MPT permission checking (step 7 of MPT lookup); XiangShan MPT hardware must NOT read mstatus.MXR during MPT access checks and must NOT allow HLVX to suppress MPT execute-fault detection, else execute-only MPT pages become readable/writable via MXR=1 or HLVX.

findings.finding: TLB permission check applies MXR to PTE-based permissions only. Stage 1: `Mux(hlvx, perm.x, perm.r || mxr(idx) && perm.x)` (line 428). Stage 2: `Mux(hlvx, g_perm.x, (g_perm.r || csr.priv.mxr && g_perm.x))` (line 443). This is spec-compliant because MPT (Smpt) is not implemented — MXR only affects page-table-encoded permissions as allowed by the spec. The RISC-V privileged spec (machine.adoc lines 633-636) explicitly states: 'The MXR and SUM mechanisms only affect the interpretation of permissions encoded in page-table entries. In particular, they have no impact on whether access-fault exceptions are raised due to PMAs or PMP.' No MPT permission table entries exist to be incorrectly overridden.
findings.snippet:
val ldPermFail = !(modeCheck && Mux(hlvx, perm.x, perm.r || mxr(idx) && perm.x))
val g_ldPermFail = !Mux(hlvx, g_perm.x, (g_perm.r || csr.priv.mxr && g_perm.x))

findings.finding: MXR value correctly computed per-port: `Mux(virt_out(i) || isHyperInst(i), csr.priv.vmxr || csr.priv.mxr, csr.priv.mxr)`. For virtualized contexts, both vmxr (VS-stage) and mxr (HS-stage) are OR'd per the hypervisor spec (hypervisor.adoc line 1473-1477): 'HS-level sstatus.MXR makes execute-only pages readable by explicit loads for both stages of address translation.' No MPT entries exist, so this cannot override MPT-encoded permissions.
findings.snippet: val mxr = (0 until Width).map(i => Mux(virt_out(i) || isHyperInst(i), csr.priv.vmxr || csr.priv.mxr, csr.priv.mxr))

findings.finding: HLVX correctly disables pointer masking (`pmm := 0.U` at line 164) and HLVX flag correctly flows to perm_check where it forces execute-permission check (perm.x) instead of MXR-augmented read check. HLVX does NOT bypass PMP checks — the PMP checker operates independently on physical addresses without any MXR influence. This matches the HLVX spec (hypervisor.adoc lines 1499-1503): 'HLVX cannot override machine-level physical memory protection (PMP), so attempting to read memory that PMP designates as execute-only still results in an access-fault exception.'

G-stage MXR permission check at line 409 correctly applies MXR only to G-stage PTE permissions: `!io.hptw.resp.bits.h_resp.entry.perm.get.r && !(io.csr.priv.mxr && io.hptw.resp.bits.h_resp.entry.perm.get.x)`. This allows MXR to make execute-only pages readable at G-stage, which is spec-compliant for PTE-based translation. No MPT table entries are involved.

Identical MXR-based G-stage permission check at line 1000 of the main PTW FSM: `!io.hptw.resp.bits.h_resp.entry.perm.get.r && !(io.csr.priv.mxr && io.hptw.resp.bits.h_resp.entry.perm.get.x)`. Same analysis as above — MXR applied to PTE-based checks only, which is correct per spec in the absence of MPT.

PMP checker is entirely independent of MXR. The `pmp_check()` function performs a pure lookup of PMP config bits (r, w, x) from matched PMP entries against the access command. No reference to mstatus.MXR exists anywhere in the PMP checker code path. This is correct per spec (machine.adoc lines 633-636): MXR 'has no impact on whether access-fault exceptions are raised due to PMAs or PMP.' HLVX executes against the PMP using the same TlbCmd-based check but with the hlvx flag handled upstream in the TLB perm_check, not in PMP.

MXR defined at bit 19 of mstatus (line 516): `CSRRWField(19).withReset(0.U)`. Bit position and reset value are correct per RISC-V privileged spec. No MPT-enable field (e.g., mptcfg or Smpt extension) is defined, consistent with MPT not being implemented.
findings.snippet: val MXR  = CSRRWField     (19).withReset(0.U).withDescription("Make executable pages readable when set.")

findings.finding: MXR correctly routed from mstatus/vsstatus CSRs to TLB: `io.tlb.mxr := mstatus.regOut.MXR.asBool` and `io.tlb.vmxr := vsstatus.regOut.MXR.asBool`. This is the single point where CSR state enters the TLB pipeline. The routing is correct — there is no MPT CSR to route.

HLVX flag correctly computed from LSUOpType: `val tlbHlvx = LSUOpType.isHlvx(tlbFuOpType)` (line 260), then wired to `io.tlbReq.bits.hlvx := tlbHlvx` (line 421). The HLVX instruction correctly sets the hlvx flag, which in TLB perm_check forces execute-permission checking (perm.x) instead of MXR-augmented read checking. No MPT interaction exists because MPT is not implemented.
